hypothesis: A scope-111 DTS is reachable by clamping the published scope-112 witness and applying small constraint-preserving mark perturbations, because the published witness may be one local move from the target boundary.
rationale: The target differs from the reproduced witness by only one scope unit; a local search can test proximity without conflating a successful exact witness with a proxy score.
expected_information_gain: Measures whether scope-111 feasibility is locally adjacent to the published witness and records the highest globally unique-difference count reached under the boundary constraint.
method: Seed with the published witness after clamping 112 to 111. Simulated annealing mutates one mark by +/-1..3, rejects non-Golomb rows through scoring, and evaluates all 105 positive differences for the best state.
metric: number of unique positive within-row differences under scope <=111
metric_relation_to_true_objective: The exact target requires 105 unique differences and scope <=111; unique-count movement below 105 is a proxy that becomes true-objective progress only when the independent validator accepts.
kill_condition: Stop after three 20-second seeds or immediately on an independently validated scope-111 witness.
interpretation: No target witness was found. All three seeds remained at the clamped published witness with 100 unique differences and five repeated differences, so the one-unit scope reduction is not locally repaired by these small single-mark moves.
what_was_learned: The clamped witness has a reproducible 100/105 unique-difference plateau; the same duplicate set [13, 36, 53, 100, 111] persists across all seeds, indicating a structured conflict rather than stochastic variance.
recommended_next_action: Do not retune this single-mark local family. Use the repeated conflict set to design a structured multi-row repair or move to an exact-cover formulation.
